# index.json is regenerated by the Scan and committed back

Images are uploaded by hand by the maintainer, so nothing else can reliably keep `index.json` in sync. The daily Scan therefore rebuilds the index from the images actually present at the repo root (the source of truth), enriches each entry with fresh Workshop metadata, and commits the result when it changed. Maps whose Workshop item has been delisted keep their previous index record — the index describes "what this repo holds", not "what the Workshop currently has". A reader seeing a CI job commit data files back into the repo should know this is deliberate, not a feedback-loop accident: the alternative (maintainer regenerates locally after every hand upload) was rejected because it adds a step that is easy to forget and produces a silently stale index.
